runtime/bytes#

The native layer under encoding/bytes, io/input: the calls those modules make into the host runtime.

Version: v1.0.0

Description#

The native layer under encoding/bytes, io/input: the calls those modules make into the host runtime. Programs use those modules instead; these declarations may change with the runtime.

Byte-range boundary for encoding/bytes. Every native reads bytes start..end of source in place, without copying them; callers check 0 <= start <= end <= source.size() first.

Public API#

native bytes_find#

native bytes_find(source is @byte, pattern is @byte, start is int) is int

First offset >= start at which pattern occurs in source, or -1. The pattern is not empty.

native bytes_utf8_invalid#

native bytes_utf8_invalid(source is @byte, start is int, end is int) is int

Offset, relative to start, of the first malformed UTF-8 scalar, or -1.

native bytes_text#

native bytes_text(source is @byte, start is int, end is int) is string

The range as a string; it is valid UTF-8.

native bytes_decimal_invalid#

native bytes_decimal_invalid(source is @byte, start is int, end is int) is int

Offset, relative to start, of the first byte that breaks an ASCII decimal integer with an optional leading '-', or -1.

native bytes_decimal#

native bytes_decimal(source is @byte, start is int, end is int) is int

The decimal value of a valid range.

native bytes_equal#

native bytes_equal(source is @byte, start is int, end is int, other is @byte) is bool

Whether the range holds exactly the bytes of other.

native bytes_integer_fits#

native bytes_integer_fits(source is @byte, start is int, end is int, signed is bool, big is bool) is bool

Fixed-width integer of a non-empty range: two's complement when signed, magnitude otherwise; big-endian when big. Fits: the value is a 64-bit int.

native bytes_integer#

native bytes_integer(source is @byte, start is int, end is int, signed is bool, big is bool) is int

The integer of source from start to end, signed or not, big- or little-endian.

native bytes_join#

native bytes_join(source is @byte, start is int, tail is @byte) is @byte

source[start..] followed by tail, as one new byte value.
